sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Media Relations and Crisis Public Relations Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada–China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c 17, and its Regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C., 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, S.C. 1988, c 45; in Quebec, the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, which mandates UBO disclosure to the Registraire des entreprises.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of General Partner (or equivalent certificate of existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Director’s Register of General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry or certified extract by corporate secretary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport Copy of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or notarized copy by a public notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Residential Address of each UBO (utility or bank statement)
Bank Reference Letter for the Limited Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the general partner

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (iii) the Canadian Economic Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; and (iv) the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) PEP list. Enhanced due diligence applies to foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) based on a risk-sensitive, 24-hour verification protocol. Screening must be repeated every 6 months and upon any material change in ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) – online via https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: In accordance with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), the name used in Quebec must have a French version for public registration and signs. The registry requires the name to be in a Roman/Latin script; transliteration into French characters is permitted, and an anglicized name must appear with a French translation in the official declaration. All documents attached to the registration must be accompanied by a certified French translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may file a written request for review with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of a rejection notice. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Cour du Québec for a declaration of validity by filing an application in the Civil Chamber within 60 days of notification. A lawyer may alternatively submit a request for an official opinion prior to filing, and the Registrar's decision is subject to judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible if the virtual office provider is a registered business centre in Quebec and maintains a physical location open for process service. For the public relations industry, a non-residential virtual office is generally acceptable; however, the Registrar may require a dedicated office address for the head office and the records of the limited partnership. The risk of rejection is moderate (10%).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate – approximately 10% annual risk of a spot-check inspection by the Registrar for compliance with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; the risk increases to 40% if the registered office is a virtual mailbox or if the enterprise fails to maintain statutory records at the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for annual virtual office lease

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, articles 2236-2266 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, sections 1-40 (registration and public disclosure)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Registre des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None – Quebec law imposes no minimum paid-up capital or escrow account requirement for limited partnerships; capital contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement and may be made in cash, kind, or industry, with the LP operable immediately upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of [●] Limited Partnership (the "Firm") hereby authorizes the formation of the Firm as a limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec and the filing of its Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the capital contributions of the limited partners, in the amounts set forth in the Limited Partnership Agreement, are hereby accepted and subscribed; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Firm is established at [●], Québec, which address is hereby adopted as the Firm's head office and registered seat; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [●] is appointed as manager and duly authorized mandatory of the Firm for the conduct of its international media relations and crisis public relations business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a statutory name search in the REQ database to confirm the proposed partnership name is distinctive and compliant with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. The name must include the compulsory suffix 'Société en commandite', 'Limited Partnership', or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'/'L.P.' as applicable. Submit an optional name reservation request to secure the approved name for 90 days before formal filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed distinctive partnership name
REQ name search confirmation report
Declaration of compulsory corporate suffix
Optional name reservation request and fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ rejects the name as non-distinctive or misleading, file a written request for review with supporting trademark or prior-use evidence, or alternatively amend the declaration to include a new distinctive element and re-file within the statutory response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel (Chambre des notaires du Québec or Chambre des avocats) acting for the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written Limited Partnership Agreement covering: identity of general and limited partners, contribution amounts and payment terms, profit/loss allocation, management authority of the general partner, restrictions on limited-partner participation in management, withdrawal and transfer provisions, and registered office address. Ensure that limited partners refrain from exercising any managerial power in order to preserve their limited liability under articles 2242-2249 C.C.Q.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (Contrat de société en commandite)
Schedule of capital contributions subscribed by each partner
Mandate of general partner if acting through a corporate representative
Acknowledgment of limited liability restrictions by limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is challenged for defective civil-law formalities or ambiguity in contribution terms, the partners may execute a corrective rider or re-execute the agreement before filing, and obtain notarization where recommended to facilitate banking or real-property opening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online filing portal (registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and electronically submit the Declaration of Registration providing: the approved partnership name, registered office address situated in Québec, name and domicile of the general partner, principal activity (NAICS 541820 – Public Relations Agencies), date of formation, and duration if not perpetual. Pay the prescribed registration fee by credit card or electronic funds transfer using the REQ secured payment interface, and retain the electronic acknowledgment with the assigned enterprise number.
required_dossiers: REQ Declaration of Registration (electronic form)
Proof of name reservation/approval
Identification document of general partner (individual: government-issued ID; legal person: certificate from REQ or extract from the relevant registry)
Registered office address confirmation in Quebec
Payment of registration fee (CAD 42)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of irregularity for missing signatures, incomplete partner information, or incompatible activity codes, remedy within the prescribed delay (typically 15-30 days) by filing an amending declaration; if the registration is refused, verify the grounds and re-file with corrected legal particulars or appeal to the administrative tribunal within the statutory limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations – Business Number, QST, GST/HST, Payroll
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – integrated new registrant registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Limited Partnership for the Quebec Business Number (NEQ-related BN), GST/HST, QST, employer payroll deductions, and the Requirement for Information return for partnerships. Complete the combined CRA/Revenu Québec new registrant package, indicating the partnership as a registrant with activity ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541820, and designate a financial institution account for remittances. For a non-resident general or limited partner, attach the relevant treaty-treatable disclosure forms.
required_dossiers: CRA Form RC1 and Revenu Québec RL-1 payroll registration data
Proof of REQ registration (enterprise number)
Partnership agreement condensation statement
Identification of each partner (name, address, SIN or BN)
Bank account details for tax remittances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If QST/GST effective-date alignment is disputed, submit a written representation to Revenu Québec with the REQ registration certificate and a timeline of first commercial activity; late registration penalties may be abated by filing a Voluntary Disclosure Agreement with CRA and Revenu Québec before any enforcement action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Establishment and Post-Registration Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Quebec municipality (borough) and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formalize the physical head office by entering into a commercial lease for the registered office and obtaining the required municipal occupancy permit confirming compliance with the Quebec Building Code and fire safety regulations. Register the establishment with CNESST within 60 days of hiring the first employee and post the certificate of establishment at the workplace. Maintain the partnership register recording contributions, transfers, partnership interests, and decisions of the general partner, and file any subsequent updates with REQ within 15 days of any change.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease agreement for registered office in Quebec
Municipal certificate of occupancy / zoning authorization
CNESST employer registration application (form E-6)
Partnership register (livre des sociétés)
Evidence of posting of establishment certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the occupancy permit for zoning non-conformity, apply for a minor variance or relocate the registered office to a compliant site; if CNESST registration was omitted, file late with a written justification and request penalty remission for first-time non-compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial license is mandated for a public relations agency (NAICS 541820) under Quebec law; the relevant administrative bodies are the municipality for occupancy/zoning permits and the Régie du bâtiment du Québec for building code compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – the only operational clearances are the municipal certificate of occupancy and, where an exterior sign is installed, a sign installation permit issued by the local borough or municipality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based media relations and communications services are not listed in Schedule I or II of the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review; no full EIA, attestation, or registration certificate is required absent industrial installation or discharge activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous air emissions are generated; the office is subject only to municipal wastewater and stormwater bylaws for sanitary and kitchenette discharges, to the residual materials recovery obligations of the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises (e-waste, batteries, lamps, paper/plastic), and to the general environmental obligation of articles 5-10 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificate of occupancy issued by the competent Quebec municipality based on compliance with the Quebec Building Code (chapter I, Building) and the Safety Code (chapter I, Safety, r. 2.1), covering means of egress, fire detection and alarm systems, emergency lighting, and barrier-free access; annual fire-safety inspection by the local fire safety service; CNESST establishment registration and employer obligations under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (CQLR c. S-2.1) and the Act respecting industrial accidents and occupational diseases (CQLR c. A-3.001), including first-aid kits, worker health and safety training, and a written prevention program where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal GST/HST and income tax administration via Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portals; Revenu Québec administers provincial income tax, the Québec Sales Tax (QST), and GST/HST collection for Québec through the clicSÉCUR Affaires portal; entity-level registration is filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), which issues the Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident limited partners: (1) register the extra-provincial limited partnership (société en commandite) with the REQ to obtain the NEQ; (2) obtain the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) through BRO or Form RC1, filed by the general partner; (3) open the GST/HST account (RTxxxxxxx) with CRA; (4) register for QST (RQ account) with Revenu Québec; (5) file annual T5013 Partnership Information Return and Québec RL-15 slips; non-resident partners additionally require a Canadian tax number and may file under ITA section 216.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Mandatory fiscal transparency under ITA s. 96; no check-the-box corporate election is available for a limited partnership under the Income Tax Act; available elections include: (i) non-resident partner election under ITA s. 216(1) to file net Canadian-source income returns; (ii) partnership fiscal period election under ITA s. 249.1; (iii) property rollover election under ITA s. 97(2) where partners transfer capital property into the LP; (iv) GST/HST joint election under ETA s. 156 for tax-exempt supplies between registrants; and (v) QST equivalent elections administered by Revenu Québec.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Value-Added Tax) and QST (Québec Sales Tax) — dual VAT regime with Revenu Québec acting as collection agent for both taxes in Québec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports) in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four consecutive quarters before GST/HST registration becomes mandatory (small supplier threshold); QST registration threshold is aligned with the GST/HST threshold for suppliers carrying on business in Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No continuous transaction control (CTC) or real-time fiscal clearance/digital stamping regime; Canada uses periodic self-assessment returns. Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST and QST returns through Revenu Québec's GST/HST Internet File Transfer service and clicSÉCUR Affaires; registrants must retain all e-invoices and source documents in machine-readable format for six years; QR-code-billed simplified invoices are permitted for amounts under CAD 150; Québec additionally mandates electronic invoicing for provincial public-sector suppliers and enhanced audit-file readability standards.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: PR retainer, media relations, crisis communications, and associated advisory services supplied to a non-resident person are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 7 (and QST equivalents), provided the service is not rendered to an individual physically present in Canada, does not relate to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of supply, and is not for the benefit of a Canadian-resident person; advertising services directed at the Canadian market remain taxable even when supplied to a non-resident; zero-rating also applies to exported physical PR collateral under Schedule VI Part I; no statutory FX repatriation deadline exists under Canadian GST/QST law — the 180-day documentary benchmark is applied by banks and CRA/Revenu Québec audit practice for export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) where physical goods accompany campaign deliverables
Signed client service agreement evidencing non-resident status and place of supply
Commercial invoice with explicit 'zero-rated export' notation and foreign client address
Bill of lading, air waybill, or courier receipt for physical media collateral
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank advice evidencing foreign-currency receipt
GST/HST registration status certificate of the foreign client, if any
Internal work papers demonstrating services were performed outside Canada and no benefit accrued to a Canadian-resident person
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rating claims within four years (indefinitely for misrepresentation), clawing back denied zero-rated status, ITCs, and QST input refunds with prescribed-rate interest compounded daily; gross negligence penalty under ETA s. 280(1) is the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax understated; false input tax credit/rebate claims attract the ETA s. 280(2) penalty of 25%; fraudulent export schemes are subject to criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 and Criminal Code s. 380 with fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years on indictment; directors, general partners, and knowingly participating limited partners may face joint and several liability for QST and GST arrears.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); FINTRAC as the AML transactional surveillance authority; Canada operates a free-float currency with no statutory FX licensing body under the Currency Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts; no exchange-control approval is required. Main constraints for a Quebec PR-firm LP are the Part XIII withholding at 25% (treaty-reduced) on guaranteed partner fees and certain non-resident remittances, and the Canadian income allocation of non-resident partners under section 96 of the Income Tax Act, which requires T5013 partnership returns. Profit remittance for a US/Europe-focused PR operation is otherwise unblocked.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export or service receipts; foreign-currency retainer proceeds may be retained indefinitely. Repatriation or conversion is subject only to FINTRAC EFT reporting at CAD 10,000 or more per incoming wire; no conversion ratio or statutory timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Constrained Medium. Wise, Revolut, Airwallex and Payoneer are legally usable as ancillary disbursement rails for sub-CAD 25,000 monthly retainer flows only if registered with FINTRAC as money-services businesses in Canada. They cannot act as the principal clearing bank for the LP because they are not Schedule I banks, do not clear through Payments Canada, and cannot hold a capital escrow designation. The treasury core must remain with a Quebec-licensed domestic bank; EMI balances should be swept monthly to the operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorised signatory must be identity-verified under Canadian PCMLTFA KYC rules. Video-verified onboarding is normally available for low-risk corporate clients with a Canadian-resident co-signer; physical branch attendance is conventionally mandated for the first non-resident signatory or for any signatory whose source of wealth is non-Canadian. Non-resident general partners do not have to travel if the account is opened by a Canadian-resident authorised agent under a general-partner resolution; full remote opening is otherwise Medium viability and adds 5-10 business days of enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered limited-partnership structure with opaque capital stack
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete LP agreement under the Civil Code of Quebec (société en commandite), REQ registration certificate, full UBO schedule for all general and limited partners, organisational chart confirming the LP is not a conduit, and a legal opinion where a non-resident corporate partner exceeds 25% of capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border retainer wires above CAD 10,000 without economic substrate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed retainer agreements, media-plan purchase orders, invoice-to-settlement mapping, FINTRAC EFT reporting log, and bank reference letters from the foreign paying bank; all wires must carry a capital-contribution or services purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative news screening of PR clients or ultimate beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Date-stamped negative-media report generated within 30 days before onboarding, enhanced due-diligence file with authoritative references, senior-manager sign-off memorandum, and semi-annual PEP re-screen where any client falls into the PEP class.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident capital contribution without evidentiary trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed source-of-wealth certificate from each contributing partner, 12-month bank statements of the contributor, audited or GAAP-abridged financial statements of the LP, contribution promissory note, and a Part XIII tax-indemnity memorandum covering non-resident remittances.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 from the foreign paying bank to a Quebec Schedule I bank (e.g., National Bank of Canada, Institution 006) through a correspondent such as BNY or JPM, with the Remittance Information narrative carrying the code CTRAT or EQUI and the text Contribution to partnership capital - no consideration. Domestic classification under the Canadian Banking Association purpose-code set should be CF. The benefit account is the LP operational or capital escrow sub-account; the receiving branch is pre-notified at T-1 for same-day contributions above CAD 1,000,000 via Payments Canada high-value clearing (LVTS/Lynx). Verification requires the signed capital-contribution resolution, 12-month contributor bank statements, and FINTRAC EFT records for every wire at CAD 10,000 or more.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 remains the default for cross-border PR retainer and vendor settlements; the US-corridor uses ACH (SEC Code CTX) for low-value and Fedwire for high-value payments, while intra-Canada high-value uses Payments Canada LVTS/Lynx and low-value instantaneous transfers use the Real-Time Rail. A commercial letter of credit (MT700) is permissible for overseas media inventory purchases against a performance certificate rather than a transport document, but invoice-based disbursement through the treasury system is preferred for PR retainers. All outgoing transfers at CAD 10,000 or more pass through the bank EFT queue with the supporting invoice uploaded to the trade-capture platform.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on USD/CAD and EUR/CAD with tenors up to 12 months under an ISDA Master Agreement with a Schedule I bank; no speculative net-short positions permitted for the PR-agency classification
Vanilla FX call and put options on USD/CAD and EUR/CAD with a licensed swap dealer or bank, with premiums settled from the operating account
Cross-currency swaps converting non-resident capital contributions into CAD without a spot leg, subject to a Credit Support Annex

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on INR/USD or CNY/USD only to hedge exact-match retainer liabilities payable to emerging-market media vendors, with bank confirmation evidencing the underlying obligation
FX swaps for funding-date alignment between inbound contribution settlement and outbound disbursement dates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of the LP's registration in the REQ register; for example, a registration anniversary of 15 March requires filing by 14 May each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the partnership to a regulated monetary penalty; continued default permits the Registrar to strike the LP from the enterprise register after prior notice, terminating its legal personality and eliminating the limited-partner liability shield.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year-end partnership, by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day, up to a maximum of CAD 500; if the return remains outstanding more than 24 months, an additional penalty of CAD 1,000 applies, together with statutory interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Relevé 15 (RL-15) partners' share of partnership income or loss
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the partnership's fiscal year-end, consistent with the T5013 due date; for a calendar-year-end partnership, by June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or failure to issue RL-15 slips to partners may result in a penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day, subject to a maximum of CAD 500, plus interest and possible criminal prosecution for wilful default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit applies to a private Quebec limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting legal publicity. An audit is required only if the partnership agreement, a creditor, a regulator, or the tax authorities (CRA/Revenu Québec) explicitly demand one; no revenue or asset threshold automatically triggers a statutory audit for a private LP.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian ASPE (Part II) for private partnerships; a consistent tax-basis framework may be used for small partnerships if accepted by CRA and Revenu Québec.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate federal or Quebec public beneficial-ownership annual filing applies to a limited partnership. The REQ annual declaration requires disclosure of general partners' names, addresses, and contributions; limited partners' identities are maintained internally and are not publicly registered. Any transfer of partnership interests must be recorded in the internal registers and reflected in the next REQ annual declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of general and limited partners
Minute book of partnership resolutions and meetings
Register of partnership interest transfers and certificates (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 80–350 per year for a Quebec registered office/agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–10,000 per year if an audit is required by a third party; typically not required for a small PR partnership
